000f8ec011:
Changed: Only a new script, reproduce_issue.py, which prints the evalf results. No library file or function was changed, and sympy/core/evalf.py was not touched.
Outcome: The fix was rejected because it failed the project's tests for this issue.
Why it failed: Evidence: test_evalf_bugs checks that NS(Mul(Max(0, y), x, evaluate=False).evalf()) == 'x*Max(0, y)'. Because evalf.py was not changed, evalf() still raises UnboundLocalError on reprec/imprec when Max comes first.
Lesson: A correct fix must change evalf() in sympy/core/evalf.py. When the real or imaginary part is not a number and no branch sets reprec/imprec, it must raise NotImplementedError, never leave them unset. evalf_mul then returns the unevaluated product whatever the argument order. A reproduction script alone does not count as a fix.
018b1b98c3:
Changed: django/db/migrations/operations/models.py, RenameIndex.database_backwards: the unnamed-index branch (old_fields) now looks up the index and renames it back to an auto-generated "_idx" name, where before it did nothing.
Outcome: The fix was rejected because it failed the project's tests for this issue.
Why it failed: Evidence: test_rename_index_unnamed_index still runs database_backwards under assertNumQueries(0) and then expects "new_pony_test_idx" to exist. The patch looks up the index and renames it, which runs queries and removes that name.
Lesson: For unnamed indexes, database_backwards must stay a no-op with zero queries. The crash has to be fixed in database_forwards: if the existing index already has the new name, re-applying must do nothing instead of trying to rename it again.
01ab2e6ffa:
Changed: lib/matplotlib/pyplot.py, switch_backend(). It no longer calls close("all") at the start. It returns early, only updating rcParams["backend"], when the current _backend_mod's FigureCanvas module matches the requested backend. Otherwise it calls close("all") just before importing the module.
Outcome: The fix was rejected because it failed the project's tests for this issue.
Why it failed: Evidence: test_no_backend_reset_rccontext sets rcParams['backend'] = 'module://aardvark' inside rc_context() and expects it to remain after the context exits. The patch never touches rc_context, which still restores the old backend value, possibly the auto sentinel, on exit.
Lesson: A correct fix must make rc_context() leave rcParams['backend'] as it is on exit, so a value set inside the context persists. Changing only switch_backend is not enough.
02bf2d0ac3:
Changed: astropy/io/fits/card.py Card.fromstring (decodes bytes input with decode_ascii before _pad; adds decode_ascii import) and astropy/io/fits/header.py Header.fromstring (decodes bytes data with decode_ascii first).
Outcome: The fix was rejected because it failed the project's tests for this issue: at least one deciding test failed, or an existing test broke.
Why it failed: Inferred: the file does not show which test failed. The patch decodes bytes as ASCII, but test_card_from_bytes says it assumes latin-1, so non-ASCII bytes would be replaced or warned about rather than kept.
Lesson: Card.fromstring and Header.fromstring must both accept bytes and str, decode bytes as latin-1 rather than strict ASCII, leave str input unchanged, pass test_card_from_bytes, and not break existing header tests.
07b5b13770:
Changed: requests/sessions.py, Session.request: replaced `method = builtin_str(method)` with `method = to_native_string(method)` and removed builtin_str from the .compat import.
Outcome: The fix was rejected because it failed the project's tests for this issue: at least one listed test failed or an existing test broke.
Why it failed: Inferred: the file does not say which test failed. The patch calls to_native_string but adds no import for it. If sessions.py does not already import it from .utils, every Session.request call raises NameError. That would break test_encoded_methods and the other listed request tests.
Lesson: In Python 3, a bytes method (b'GET') must be decoded to the str 'GET', never turned into "b'GET'". Every helper the fix uses must be imported in sessions.py, and requests.request(b'GET', url) must return ok.
0a42bb6340:
Changed: sphinx/ext/autodoc/__init__.py, Documenter.filter_members (adds a lookup of attr_docs when doc is None). Also pins dependencies in setup.py and adds -rA to tox.ini, which is unrelated to the issue.
Outcome: The fix was rejected because it failed the project's tests for this issue.
Why it failed: Inferred: the new lines sit inside the `if isinstance(obj, ObjectMember) and obj.docstring:` block, where doc has just been set to a truthy docstring. So `doc is None` is never true and the code never runs. The `#: :meta public:` comment on a module variable never reaches extract_metadata, and test_private_field and test_private_members still hide _PUBLIC_CONSTANT.
Lesson: When a member has no docstring of its own, the private/public check must read the `#:` comment from attr_docs, for every member. With only :members:, _PUBLIC_CONSTANT must be shown and PRIVATE_CONSTANT hidden.
0ab040e16d:
Changed: lib/matplotlib/contour.py: ContourSet._process_contour_level_args (new z_dtype parameter) and QuadContourSet._contour_args (keeps the input's dtype before the float64 conversion).
Outcome: The fix was rejected because it failed the project's tests for this issue.
Why it failed: Evidence: test_bool_autolevel expects contourf on bool input (list, ndarray, masked) to give levels [0, .5, 1], but the patch skips filled contours and leaves 7 auto levels. The patch also only touched QuadContourSet, so tricontour and tricontourf on bool z get no special levels.
Lesson: With no levels given on bool z, line contours must default to [0.5] and filled contours to [0, 0.5, 1]. This must work for lists, ndarrays and masked arrays, and in both the quad (contour/contourf) and tri (tricontour/tricontourf) code paths.
0ae54276ad:
Changed: sympy/printing/latex.py, LatexPrinter.__init__ (how mul_symbol_latex and mul_symbol_latex_numbers are set); also added stray scripts edit_mul_symbol.py, fix_mul_symbol.py, run_mul_symbol_tests.py, test_mul_symbol.py at the repo root.
Outcome: The fix was rejected because it failed the project's tests for this issue (test_latex_basic).
Why it failed: Inferred: for a custom mul_symbol, the patch also uses the raw symbol as mul_symbol_latex_numbers. So latex(1.5*3**x, mul_symbol='\\,') gives "1.5\,3^{x}", but test_latex_basic expects "1.5 \cdot 3^{x}".
Lesson: An arbitrary mul_symbol string must be inserted exactly as given between factors ("3\,x^{2}\,y"). The separator between two numbers must still fall back to the 'dot' entry (" \cdot ") for any symbol not in the table, as it does for None.
0c600ea3eb:
Changed: django/contrib/admin/options.py: InlineModelAdmin.get_formset (extra set to 0 without add permission), has_add_permission, has_change_permission and has_delete_permission (auto-created branch). Also added a stray root script, reproduce_error.py.
Outcome: The fix passed the issue's tests, but wider tests and review later found it wrong. No failing test is on record.
Why it failed: Inferred: the auto-created branch returns only from a loop over fields whose remote model is not the parent model. For a self-referential M2M, no field matches, so the code falls through to super() and checks permissions the auto-created model doesn't have. It also requires change permission on the parent model as well as the target model, and ignores obj.
Lesson: A correct fix must make inlines for auto-created M2M models read-only for users with only view permission. It must base add/change/delete on change permission for the related target model, must handle self-referential M2M, and must not commit scratch scripts.
0e63727d0e:
Changed: sympy/core/exprtools.py factor_terms inner do() (the "< 0" check became .is_negative); sympy/matrices/matrices.py _eval_det_bareiss (falls back to _eval_det_berkowitz when the result has S.NaN).
Outcome: The fix was rejected because it failed the project's tests for this issue (test_determinant).
Why it failed: Inferred: Bareiss still pivots on symbolic entries that are really zero but not seen as zero, so it divides by zero. Hiding the comparison error and checking only for NaN at the end misses zoo or wrong results. So det() of M(5), M(6) and M(7) with entries i + a*j does not reliably give exactly 0.
Lesson: A correct fix must stop Bareiss from choosing or dividing by a pivot that is symbolically zero, and M(n).det() for n=5,6,7 must return exactly 0. Masking the NaN comparison or post-checking for NaN is not enough.
0e88337abb:
Changed: requests/sessions.py, Session.request: replaced `method = builtin_str(method)` with `method = to_native_string(method)`; also added a top-level reproduce_issue.py script that makes live httpbin.org calls.
Outcome: The fix passed the project's tests for this issue but wider tests and review later found it wrong; no failing test is on record.
Why it failed: Inferred: to_native_string only handles str/bytes. Any other method object that builtin_str used to accept (e.g. a custom str-like type) now raises instead of being converted, and non-ASCII bytes fail on decode. The patch also ships an unrelated script that needs the network.
Lesson: Decode only when the method is bytes. Keep builtin_str conversion for every other type so behaviour is unchanged. Python 2 str and unicode must stay native. Do not add repro scripts to the repo.
138d83ab2f:
Changed: sympy/geometry/point.py, Point.__new__ (the imaginary-coordinate check now runs only when evaluate is True); also added a stray script, reproduce_error.py, at the repo root.
Outcome: The fix passed the project's tests for this issue, but wider tests and review later found it wrong; no failing test is on record.
Why it failed: Inferred: the patch turns off the imaginary-coordinate check whenever evaluate is False, so Point(1+I, 2, evaluate=False) or Point2D(I, 1) inside evaluate(False) is now accepted. The real cause is not addressed: under global evaluate(False), im(a) stays an unevaluated im(...) object, which is always truthy.
Lesson: A correct fix must still reject truly imaginary coordinates in every evaluate mode. It must accept real coordinates under evaluate(False) and must not treat an unevaluated im(a) as truthy. It must not add scratch files.
164f21d7af:
Changed: src/_pytest/mark/structures.py: get_unpacked_marks() (new consider_mro=True parameter; for a class it walks __mro__ and reads each class's own __dict__["pytestmark"]) and store_mark() (now calls it with consider_mro=False).
Outcome: The fix was rejected because it failed the project's tests for this issue, either test_mark_mro or an existing test.
Why it failed: Inferred: on my reading, test_mark_mro ([c, a, b] and [c]) passes, so an existing test probably broke. Reading only __dict__ drops marks that a class exposes through a metaclass property or a non-dict attribute, and a subclass's own pytestmark no longer replaces its bases' marks.
Lesson: A correct fix must return the class's own marks first, then each base's marks once in MRO order, keep consider_mro=False to the class's own marks only, and leave non-class objects and existing class-mark tests unchanged.
167ab989a0:
Changed: sphinx/ext/autodoc/__init__.py (PropertyDocumenter.can_document_member, new PropertyDocumenter.import_object unwrapping classmethod(property)); sphinx/ext/autodoc/importer.py (get_class_members, MRO lookup); also pinned dependencies in setup.py and edited tox.ini.
Outcome: The fix was rejected because it failed the project's tests for this issue (at least one listed test failed, or an existing test broke).
Why it failed: Evidence: test_pyproperty expects py:property to accept a :classmethod: option and render "class property "; test_properties and test_class_properties expect autodoc to emit ":classmethod:" for Foo.prop2. The patch never changes the Python domain or the directive header, so neither output appears.
Lesson: A correct fix must add a :classmethod: option to py:property (rendered "class property ") and make PropertyDocumenter detect classmethod-wrapped properties and emit that option. It must not change dependency pins.
16d1c80754:
Changed: sympy/matrices/common.py: hstack and vstack (new shortcut for when every argument has 0 rows or 0 cols), row_join (null-matrix branch rewritten); also added reproduce_error.py.
Outcome: The fix passed the issue's tests but wider tests and review later found it wrong; no failing test is on record.
Why it failed: Inferred: the shortcuts only cover the case where every argument is empty, and they build the result with cls._new instead of type(args[0]). The row_join rewrite behaves the same as before, col_join is untouched, and direct row_join/col_join calls on zero-size matrices (including any subclass overrides, such as sparse ones) stay broken.
Lesson: A correct fix must make the per-pair row_join and col_join (and any subclass overrides) add up the dimensions of zero-size matrices, keep the type of the first argument, and not depend on special cases inside hstack or vstack.
1798bf476b:
Changed: django/db/models/base.py, Model._save_table: added "pk_val is None" to the force_insert condition, plus duplicate force_insert lines, blank lines, a stray file named 'django/db/models/base.py"', and scripts reproduce_issue.py and test_fix.py.
Outcome: It passed the project's tests for this issue, but wider tests and review later found it wrong. No failing test is on record.
Why it failed: Inferred: by the time this check runs, _save_table has already filled pk_val from the field default when it was None. So pk_val is never None when there is a default, and the check never fires. That removes the skip-UPDATE behaviour for all instances whose pk came from the default, instead of only for instances given an explicit pk.
Lesson: The fix must decide whether the pk was set explicitly before the default is applied. It must keep the forced INSERT for pks that came from the default, do UPDATE-then-INSERT for explicit pks, and also cover loaddata re-runs. It must not add stray files.
1905e96ec2:
Changed: django/db/models/enums.py, where ChoicesMeta.__new__ now sets cls.do_not_call_in_templates = True, IntegerChoices is rebased onto enum.IntEnum and TextChoices onto (str, enum.Enum), each with its own __str__. It also adds a stray reproduce_error.py at the repo root.
Outcome: The fix passed the issue's tests but wider tests and review found it wrong. No failing test is on record.
Why it failed: Inferred: IntegerChoices and TextChoices no longer inherit from Choices, so isinstance(x, Choices) checks and Choices behaviour break for them, and IntegerChoices now gets IntEnum semantics instead of (int, Choices).
Lesson: Make Choices classes not callable in templates (do_not_call_in_templates) without changing the class hierarchy. IntegerChoices must stay (int, Choices) and TextChoices (str, Choices). Add no scratch files.
1c86650c5c:
Changed: django/forms/models.py: BaseInlineFormSet.add_fields (passes initial=None instead of nulling the parent's defaulted key) and InlineForeignKeyField.__init__ (skips the parent value when initial is given).
Outcome: The fix was rejected because it failed the project's tests for this issue.
Why it failed: Inferred: the patch no longer clears the parent's key in any case. A defaulted UUID primary key therefore survives a submit, but test_inlineformset_factory_ignores_default_pks_on_submit now asserts that formset.instance.uuid and the child's parent_id are None.
Lesson: When the parent is being added, keep setting a defaulted primary key to None. Do not clear a defaulted non-pk to_field key when form data is bound: it must stay set and match the child's FK. With no data, the alternate-key field's initial must still be None.
1c9e7d90f4:
Changed: sphinx/ext/autodoc/__init__.py Documenter.filter_members (reads analyzer attr_docs when doc is empty); sphinx/util/docstrings.py extract_metadata (new '#:' branch and a loose ':meta ' parser) and prepare_commentdoc (appends ':' to ':meta' lines); adds a stray reproduce_error.py.
Outcome: Passed the issue's tests but wider tests and review later found it wrong; no failing test is on record.
Why it failed: Inferred: the '#:' comment is used only when the member has no docstring of its own, so values carrying their own __doc__ ignore ':meta public:'. The shared docstring helpers also change for every docstring: comment text is rewritten, and loose ':meta' lines get parsed.
Lesson: Read metadata from a variable's '#:' comment whenever one exists. Leave the general parsing and rendering helpers unchanged, and add no scratch files.
1d3d934b0f:
Changed: sympy/printing/conventions.py, only the module-level regex _name_with_digits_p used by split_super_sub. It became ^([^\W\d_]+)([0-9]+)$ with re.UNICODE, so Unicode letters now count as the name but the digit part was still ASCII [0-9].
Outcome: The fix was rejected because it failed the project's tests for this issue: at least one decisive test failed, or an existing test broke.
Why it failed: Evidence: test_super_sub expects non-ASCII Unicode digits to split off as subscripts, for example "w𝟙" -> ("w", [], ["𝟙"]), "w𝟙2𝟙", "ω𝟙^α" and "ω𝟙2^3α" -> ("ω", ["3α"], ["𝟙2"]). [0-9] does not match 𝟙, so these names stay unsplit.
Lesson: A correct fix must treat any Unicode letter run as the name and any Unicode decimal-digit run (\d, or mixed digits like 𝟙2𝟙) as the trailing subscript. It must also keep the ASCII results, such as w1 -> w, ["1"], unchanged.
1d4abbc194:
Changed: django/forms/models.py construct_instance(). The fix deleted the has_default() / value_omitted_from_data() skip and put a duplicated comment in its place. It also added stray files: models.py.backup, my_test_settings.py, reproduce_issue.py and run_tests.py.
Outcome: Rejected because it failed the project's tests for this issue (at least one target test failed, or an existing test broke).
Why it failed: Evidence: in test_default_not_populated_on_non_empty_value_in_cleaned_data, the subTests that put each empty value in cleaned_data['mode'] expect the model default 'di'. With the skip removed, the empty value overwrites the default.
Lesson: When a field with a default is missing from POST data, use cleaned_data only if the value is not in the form field's empty_values; otherwise keep the default. Keep the checkbox exception, and add no stray files.
1da34d63d4:
Changed: django/core/management/base.py (BaseCommand.create_parser now adds --skip-checks to every command); django/core/management/commands/runserver.py (Command.inner_run skips check() and check_migrations() when skip_checks is set); added a stray root-level script, test_management.py.
Outcome: The fix passed the project's tests for this issue but wider tests and review later found it wrong; no failing test is on record.
Why it failed: Inferred: it adds --skip-checks to every command, including commands with requires_system_checks=False, where the flag does nothing and only clutters help and parsing. It also changes runserver's own check logic, which the issue did not ask for, and leaves a debug script in the repository.
Lesson: Show --skip-checks only on commands that run system checks (requires_system_checks). Keep call_command's skip_checks default unchanged, and do not add stray files or unrelated behaviour changes.
1e54ebbac8:
Changed: django/db/models/base.py, Model._check_ordering (the related-field loop): adds `if part == "pk": break` before get_field.
Outcome: The fix was rejected because it failed the project's tests for this issue (one or more decisive tests failed, or an existing test broke).
Why it failed: Inferred: It only skips "pk". When a part resolves to a non-relation field, the loop keeps using the previous model. So 'parent__field1__field2' resolves field2 on Parent, and no E015 is raised. test_ordering_pointing_multiple_times_to_model_fields expects E015 for this. Breaking on "pk" also ignores any parts after it without checking them.
Lesson: Resolve "pk" as the current model's primary key, so 'parent__pk' passes. After a non-relation field, a later part must be accepted only if it is a valid transform/lookup of that field; otherwise raise E015. Never silently skip parts.
20fe6bce5b:
Changed: django/forms/models.py: BaseModelFormSet (__init__ takes can_add, clean, save_new_objects), modelformset_factory and inlineformset_factory (new can_add=True argument). Also removed blank lines throughout the file and added a stray test_settings.py.
Outcome: Rejected; it failed the project's tests for this issue.
Why it failed: Evidence: test_edit_only, test_edit_only_inlineformset_factory and test_edit_only_object_outside_of_queryset call the factories with edit_only=True, a keyword the patch never adds. Even with the name fixed, clean() raises a "cannot_add" ValidationError for changed extra forms, while the tests expect is_valid() to be True.
Lesson: Both factories must accept edit_only=True. With it set, extra forms are ignored without error. save() must create no new objects, including for a submitted pk outside the queryset, and edits to existing objects must still save.
213f545562:
Changed: new astropy/coordinates/builtin_frames/itrs_observed_transforms.py (itrs_to_observed_mat, itrs_to_observed, observed_to_itrs, with a 100,000 km distance cutoff that falls back to CIRS), the import in builtin_frames/__init__.py, and a setuptools pin in pyproject.toml.
Outcome: Rejected; it failed the project's tests for this issue.
Why it failed: Evidence: test_itrs_topo_to_altaz_with_refraction, test_itrs_topo_to_hadec_with_refraction, test_cirs_itrs_topo and test_itrs_straight_overhead all build ITRS(location=loc) (or ITRS(..., location=home)). The patch never adds a location attribute to ITRS and never handles topocentric ITRS. It also applies no refraction on the direct path.
Lesson: A correct fix must give ITRS a location attribute, support topocentric ITRS through CIRS<->ITRS and ITRS<->AltAz/HADec, apply refraction when pressure is set, and round-trip without a distance heuristic.
214fa3e4f0:
Changed: django/core/management/commands/inspectdb.py, Command.handle_inspection: added cached helpers get_relations, get_primary_key_column and get_column_to_field_name, and set extra_params['to_field'] when a foreign key references a column that is not the target's primary key.
Outcome: The fix was rejected because it failed the project's tests for this issue: at least one decisive test failed, or an existing test broke.
Why it failed: Inferred: test_foreign_key_to_field expects to_field='people_unique_id', which is the raw column name of the referenced column. The patch passes that column through normalize_col_name as a relation column, so the "_id" is removed and the output is to_field='people_unique'.
Lesson: When the referenced column is not the primary key, a correct fix emits to_field with the referenced column's name exactly as the database reports it. It must not rename that column into a Python attribute name.
272a27437f:
Changed: django/forms/boundfield.py, BoundWidget.id_for_label. It now returns self.data['attrs'].get('id'), and falls back to 'id_%s_%s' % (name, index) when no id is set.
Outcome: The fix was rejected because it failed the project's tests for this issue: at least one decisive test failed or an existing test broke.
Why it failed: Evidence: test_iterable_boundfield_select uses BeatleForm(auto_id=False) and expects fields[0].id_for_label to be None. The patch's fallback returns 'id_name_0' instead.
Lesson: BoundWidget.id_for_label must return exactly the id in self.data['attrs'], so auto_id='prefix_%s' gives 'prefix_field_0'. When no id is set (auto_id=False), it must return None and must not build an 'id_<name>_<index>' fallback.
281c465dc9:
Changed: django/core/management/base.py, BaseCommand.create_parser (adds a store_true --skip-checks argument), plus a new stray script, reproduce_error.py, at the repo root.
Outcome: The fix passed the project's tests for this issue, but wider tests and review later found it wrong. No failing test is on record.
Why it failed: Inferred: --skip-checks is added to every command, even commands with requires_system_checks False, where it does nothing. 'skip_checks' stays in base_stealth_options even though it is now a real option. The help ordering is not updated. A debug script is committed.
Lesson: Add --skip-checks only when the command runs system checks (requires_system_checks). Treat it as a real option rather than a stealth one. Keep execute()/call_command skip behaviour the same. Add no stray files.
2935c33127:
Changed: astropy/io/fits/card.py. In Card._split, the CONTINUE branch now reads each subcard's card.value and card.comment instead of matching _strg_comment_RE. It drops the fallback that returned unmatched cards verbatim and re-escapes quotes when it rebuilds the value. 2a6fa0bb80:
Changed: django/db/models/expressions.py, adding @deconstructible(path='django.db.models.<Name>') to Func, Value, ExpressionList, ExpressionWrapper, When, Case, Subquery, Exists, OrderBy, Window and WindowFrame. It also added a stray reproduce_error.py at the repository root.

If deconstructible applies the path to every subclass, then subclasses of Func (Lower, Coalesce, Avg) and of Subquery or Expression would deconstruct as django.db.models.Func and so on. 2cc25726b8:
Changed: lib/matplotlib/dates.py, _wrap_in_tex(). It dropped the regex that keeps letter runs outside math and now wraps the whole text as $\mathdefault{...}$ with only '-' replaced by '{-}'. It also added scratch scripts and test_output.png.
Outcome: The fix was rejected because it failed the project's tests for this issue.
Why it failed: Evidence: test_date_formatter_usetex[delta2/delta3] expect spaces as '\;' and colons as '{:}' (e.g. '01\;00{:}05'), and the patch leaves both unchanged. test_concise_formatter_usetex[t_delta2/t_delta3] expect '04{:}00' and 'Jan$\mathdefault{{-}01}$', but the patch outputs '04:00' and puts 'Jan' inside the math.
Lesson: _wrap_in_tex must keep letter runs (like month names) outside math mode, write '-' as '{-}', ':' as '{:}' and spaces as '\;', and drop empty $\mathdefault{}$ groups.
2ce004535a:
Changed: django/contrib/admin/options.py, BaseModelAdmin.lookup_allowed(). It changed the relation_parts condition so that a part is kept when the field is a primary-key OneToOneField, even if it is in prev_field's target_fields.
Outcome: The fix passed the tests for this issue, but wider tests and review later found it wrong. No failing test is on record.
Why it failed: Inferred: the fix checks for OneToOneField with primary_key=True, but multi-table inheritance parent links (the *_ptr fields) are also primary-key OneToOneFields. So the fix also stops collapsing inheritance lookups and changes which of those lookups are allowed.
Lesson: A correct fix must keep a primary-key OneToOneField that is not a parent link as a real relation step, such as restaurant__place__country. It must still collapse concrete-inheritance parent links (fields in model._meta.parents) and target-field shortcuts such as employee__department__id.
2d642a957f:
Changed: django/template/defaultfilters.py, the add() filter (new except TypeError branch that calls force_str on both operands when either is a Promise), plus force_str/Promise imports.
Outcome: The fix was rejected because it failed the project's tests for this issue (at least one decisive test failed or an existing test broke).
Why it failed: Inferred: the patch only works around the problem inside the add filter and leaves django/utils/functional.py alone, so lazy proxies still cannot do "+" themselves. test_lazy_add (lazy(lambda: 4, int)() + lazy(lambda: 5, int)() == 9) cannot pass.
Lesson: The fix must make lazy proxy objects support addition directly (an __add__/__radd__ that evaluates the proxy), for any result type including int, so that test_add08/test_add09 ('stringlazy') and test_lazy_add pass. A filter-only workaround that converts to str is not enough.
2d7191389d:
Changed: seaborn/_core/plot.py: Plotter._finalize_figure (turns off the grid for Nominal axes, sets limits to -0.5..n-0.5 from the tick count, inverts a nominal y axis); adds _pandas_inf_as_na and uses it in the subplot data filtering.
Outcome: Rejected; it failed the project's tests for this issue (at least one decisive test failed or an existing test broke).

2dfc361d9c:
Changed: sphinx/domains/cpp.py: added _udl_suffix_re and a new ASTUserDefinedLiteral class, and changed DefinitionParser._parse_literal for number, string and char literals. It also pinned dependencies in setup.py and changed the pytest flags in tox.ini.
Outcome: Rejected; it failed the project's tests for this issue.
Why it failed: Evidence: tests/test_domain_cpp.py::test_expressions expects ids like 'clL_Zli4_udlEL5EE', a call to operator"" with the literal as argument. The patch's get_id returns 'udl'+literal+suffix instead. Its parser also lets the u/l/f suffix loop run first, so '5uludl' and '5.0fudl' split the suffix wrongly.
Lesson: The id must be cl + L_Zli<len><suffix>E + the literal id + E. A suffix after a number must be parsed as one whole UDL identifier, not first eaten by the built-in u/l/f suffixes.
2f00965a4e:
Changed: django/core/management/__init__.py, call_command(): added a loop over parser._mutually_exclusive_groups. Also added a stray reproduce_error.py script.
Outcome: The fix passed the issue's tests but wider tests and review later found it wrong, and no failing test is on record.
Why it failed: Inferred: it acts on every mutually exclusive group, required or not. Any group option passed as a kwarg goes to parse_args as '--opt=value', so store_true or store_const options become '--flag=True', which argparse rejects. It also raises a new hand-made CommandError for non-required groups that used to work.
Lesson: Forward a kwarg to parse_args only when its option belongs to a group with required=True. Leave non-required groups unchanged, and never put '=value' on options that take no argument.
32bb3b64e3:
Changed: xarray/core/dataarray.py, DataArray.to_unstacked_dataset (sel with drop=True, skips empty selections, passes attrs=self.attrs to Dataset); added a stray reproduce.py at the repository root.
Outcome: The fix passed the project's tests for this issue, but wider tests and review later found it wrong; no failing test is on record.
Why it failed: Inferred: besides adding drop=True, it changes other behaviour. Any variable whose selection is empty is silently left out of the result. The stacked DataArray's attrs are copied onto the returned Dataset. It also commits a scratch script and changes whitespace.
Lesson: The roundtrip for single-dim variables must work by dropping the conflicting stacked-coordinate leftovers on each selected variable. The fix must not silently drop variables, must not change the result's attrs, and must not add files outside the fix.
337093719f:
Changed: django/db/migrations/operations/models.py: it added reduce() to AlterTogetherOptionOperation, AlterUniqueTogether and AlterIndexTogether.
Outcome: The fix passed the project's tests for this issue, but wider tests and review later found it wrong, and no failing test is on record.
Why it failed: Inferred: the subclass reduce() methods call super(ModelOperation, self).reduce(), which skips ModelOptionOperation.reduce and ModelOperation.reduce. As a result, an AlterUniqueTogether or AlterIndexTogether followed by a DeleteModel of the same model no longer collapses into the DeleteModel. The subclass overrides also leave the base reduce() unused.
Lesson: A correct fix must keep the existing parent reduce chain: same-class merging, absorption by DeleteModel, and passing through operations that do not reference the model. It may only add a rule that lets AlterUniqueTogether and AlterIndexTogether on the same model optimize through each other.
339706446a:
Changed: sklearn/linear_model/least_angle.py, LassoLarsIC.fit (copy_X default changed to None, docstring updated, new local copy_X_ added); also added the scripts reproduce_issue.py and test_copy_x_fix.py.
Outcome: The fix was rejected because it failed the project's tests for this issue.
Why it failed: Evidence: test_lasso_lars_fit_copyX_behaviour[False] failed. fit computes copy_X_ but never uses it. _preprocess_data still receives self.copy_X (default True), so X is copied even when fit is called with copy_X=False. lars_path still gets the raw fit argument, which can be None.
Lesson: Resolve one value (the fit argument if given, otherwise self.copy_X) and pass that value to both _preprocess_data and lars_path. An explicit fit(copy_X=False) must let X be overwritten, and a constructor copy_X=False must hold when fit gets no copy_X.
39376636c5:

39ff7bcfb9:
Changed: lib/matplotlib/axes/_base.py, _AxesBase.set_ylim only. It records is_inverted = bottom > top in the log branch and swaps the limits back after nonsingular/limit_range_for_scale.
Outcome: The fix passed the project's tests for this issue, but wider tests and review later found it wrong. No failing test is on record.

It also takes the direction before non-positive limits are swapped for old values, so it can flip the axis the wrong way.
Lesson: A correct fix must keep the requested order (lower > upper) on both the x and y axes for log scales. It should do this where the reordering happens (locator nonsingular / limit_range_for_scale), not through a y-only swap afterwards.
3bb68b3cdb:
Changed: sklearn/utils/_set_output.py: _wrap_in_pandas_container (new dtypes argument, astype applied) and _wrap_data_with_container (always builds dtypes from original_input for output columns); also added stray reproduce_dtype.py.
Outcome: Passed the issue's tests but was later found wrong by wider tests and review; no failing test is on record.
Why it failed: Inferred: dtype preservation is unconditional for every pandas-output transformer, with no opt-in. Transformers that change values (scalers, imputers) get results cast back to input dtypes such as int, float16 or category, which loses data, gives NaN or raises. It also changes default behaviour.
Lesson: Preservation must be opt-in (for example a set_output option), off by default. It applies only when requested, to unchanged output columns. Leave default dtypes unchanged and commit no scratch scripts.
42cf207ab5:
Changed: sympy/core/function.py, Function._eval_evalf (the _imp_ fallback branch); also added the scratch scripts reproduce_error.py and test_complex_cases.py.
Outcome: The fix passed the project's tests for this issue, but wider tests and review later found it wrong. No failing test is on record.
Why it failed: Inferred: it calls result.evalf(prec), but prec in _eval_evalf is binary precision while evalf() expects decimal digits, so results get the wrong precision. It can also return a non-numeric expression instead of a Float or None. The args are still passed to _imp_ unevaluated, so lambdas that need numbers (for example, math functions) still fail.
Lesson: A correct fix must evalf each argument at prec before calling _imp_, must keep the binary-precision semantics (no evalf(prec) with binary prec), and must return a Float or None.
47856a277c:
Changed: sympy/core/numbers.py Float.__eq__ (a zero Float now returns False for a Boolean); sympy/logic/boolalg.py added BooleanFalse.__eq__ (False for Float/Integer, otherwise Basic.__eq__); also added a stray reproduce_error.py at the repo root.
Outcome: Passed the issue's tests but wider tests and review found it wrong; no failing test is on record.
Why it failed: Inferred: the new BooleanFalse.__eq__ only covers Float/Integer and BooleanFalse, so the comparison logic is now split and lopsided. Its except clause uses SympifyError, which boolalg may not import. It also commits a debug script.
Lesson: S(0.0)==S.false and S.false==S(0.0) must both be False, matching S(0). Fix it in the numeric __eq__ without a one-sided override on BooleanFalse, and add no stray files.
48a645be37:
Changed: sphinx/ext/autodoc/__init__.py: added DataDocumenterMixinBase._has_doc_comment; GenericAliasMixin, NewTypeMixin and TypeVarMixin update_content skip "alias of" when a doc-comment exists.
Outcome: Rejected; it failed the project's tests for this issue.

It expects the doc-comment and no "alias of" line. The patch never touches ClassDocumenter's alias path, so that path still emits "alias of :class:`target.classes.Bar`" or ignores the comment.
Lesson: A correct fix must make ClassDocumenter (class aliases) as well as the data mixins prefer a #: or trailing-string doc-comment over the "alias of ..." default text, and print the comment's text.
49260b4c44:
Changed: django/db/migrations/serializer.py, TypeSerializer.serialize: switched __name__ to __qualname__ and added an import for the models.Model case. It also added stray repro files (reproduce.py, reproduce/, reproduce_settings.py, test1/).

Lesson: A correct fix must give the full __qualname__ in the dotted path that Field.deconstruct() returns, so an inner Field subclass becomes module.Outer.Inner. Fixing TypeSerializer alone is not enough, and the patch must not add stray repro files.
498b274710:
Changed: sympy/tensor/array/dense_ndim_array.py, the two _new constructors (ImmutableDenseNDimArray, MutableDenseNDimArray), where _loop_size for an empty shape went from 0 to 1; also added a stray root script reproduce_issue.py that imports numpy.
Outcome: Passed the issue's tests but wider tests and review found it wrong; no failing test is on record.

Lesson: A correct fix makes len() return 1 for every rank-0 array type (dense and sparse, mutable and immutable). It does this wherever _loop_size is computed for shape (), and it adds no stray scripts or numpy dependency.
54f6d0de53:
Changed: sphinx/ext/autodoc/__init__.py, in Documenter.add_content (looks up base-class attr docs through the MRO) and Documenter.filter_members (attr_docs_by_namespace for base classes).
Outcome: Rejected; it failed the project's tests for this issue, or an existing test broke.
Why it failed: Inferred: test_inherited_instance_variable expects Bar.attr1 ("docstring foo"), an instance attribute set only in Foo.__init__. The patch only filters and documents members that are already listed. It never changes how members are collected (get_object_members/get_class_members), which read analyzer attr docs only under Bar's own qualname, so attr1 is likely never listed.
Lesson: With inherited-members, member collection itself must add doc-commented instance attributes from every base class in the MRO, keyed by that base's qualname. A subclass's own comment must win: Bar.attr2 shows "docstring bar".
556dfacd54:
Changed: django/forms/fields.py, MultiValueField.clean(). It split the "all subvalues empty" check and skipped the early empty return when require_all_fields=False and a subfield is required.

Lesson: A correct fix must make validation and rendering both follow each subfield's own required flag when require_all_fields=False. Only required subfields' widgets get the "required" attribute. A patch that changes only clean() is not enough.
5689358d6c:
Changed: pylint/config/__init__.py: the PYLINT_HOME selection (new _expand_path, LEGACY_PYLINT_HOME), _get_pdata_path (new pylint_home parameter), load_results (falls back to legacy ~/.pylint.d), save_results (makedirs); also doc/faq.rst and the ENV_HELP text.

Lesson: When PYLINTHOME is unset and home resolves, PYLINT_HOME must equal appdirs.user_cache_dir("pylint") on every OS. That is a cache directory, not a data directory, and has no Windows special case. When home is "~", it stays ".pylint.d".
573ce7d1fc:
Changed: sympy/combinatorics/homomorphisms.py, inner function _image() used by _check_homomorphism: it dropped the PermutationGroup branch that mapped r[i] to domain.generators via gens.index and now always uses s = r[i]. It also added a reproduce_error.py script at the repository root.
Outcome: The fix passed the project's tests for this issue, but wider tests and review later found it wrong. No failing test is on record.
Why it failed: Inferred: s = r[i] is a free-group symbol from the presentation, not a Permutation. Lookups in images, which is keyed by the domain's permutations, can miss or match the wrong entry, so relators are not evaluated correctly. The inverted-generator case is still not handled.
Lesson: A correct fix must map every relator symbol, inverted ones included, to the matching domain generator or its inverse, with the right exponent sign, before looking it up in images. It must not just drop that mapping.
585dadd8d8:
Changed: sphinx/ext/napoleon/docstring.py, adding NumpyDocstring._consume_fields, which splits comma-separated names into separate fields; also setup.py dependency pins, tox.ini, and stray root test_*.py/examine_test.py scripts.

Why it failed: Evidence: test_multiple_parameters expects "**x1, x2** (:class:`array_like`)" as one combined entry when napoleon_use_param=False. The patch always splits the names, so it gives two entries. The test also expects types rendered as :class:`...`, and the patch never touches type formatting.
Lesson: Split "x1, x2" into separate :param:/:type: pairs only when napoleon_use_param=True. Keep the names combined in the field list otherwise. Render NumPy types as :class:`type`. Never split *args, **kwargs. Leave out the unrelated files and dependency pins.
58826826cc:
Changed: django/contrib/admin/options.py, ModelAdmin.get_search_results (now ANDs the per-term OR Q objects and calls a single queryset.filter()). The patch also adds unrelated files: server.log, binary test.db, a testapp/ package (models, admin, migrations) and tests/__init__.py.

Why it failed: Inferred: the search change itself joins once per relation, but the patch also commits a debug log, a database file, a scratch app, and a tests/__init__.py that turns Django's tests directory into a package, which can break test discovery.
Lesson: Apply all search terms in one filter() so multi-valued lookups join only once, and change only options.py (plus real tests). Do not add logs, databases, scratch apps or package markers.
58f0b79120:
Changed: src/_pytest/reports.py: the import line, BaseReport._to_json (new ExceptionChainRepr branch that writes "type"/"chain"/"sections", with chains of length 1 collapsed to the old format) and BaseReport._from_json (rebuilds ExceptionChainRepr); also committed helper scripts, test files and reports.py.backup.

There is a stray "):(self.longrepr, ..." after the new elif in _to_json and duplicated condition lines in _from_json, so the module does not import and test_chained_exceptions[TestReport/CollectReport] cannot pass.

5c886403ba:
Changed: django/utils/autoreload.py, get_child_arguments(), which now adds '-X%s%s' % (k, ('=' + v) if v else '') for each entry in sys._xoptions. It also added a stray reproduce_error.py file.
Outcome: The fix passed the project's tests for this issue but wider tests and review later found it wrong, because it does not correctly resolve the issue.
Why it failed: Inferred: a flag given without a value, such as -X utf8, is stored in sys._xoptions as True, not as a string. Because True is truthy, the patch evaluates '=' + True, which raises TypeError, so the reloader crashes in exactly the case the issue reports. The patch's own reproduce script checks for bool, but the real code does not.
Lesson: For each sys._xoptions entry, a correct fix must emit '-Xkey' when the value is True and '-Xkey=value' when it is a string. It must never join a str with a bool. It must also leave -W handling and the rest of the child arguments unchanged.
5ca6217228:
Changed: django/db/models/expressions.py Exists.as_sql (catches EmptyResultSet and returns '1=1' when negated); sql/compiler.py SQLCompiler.as_sql (shape-based '1=1' instead of '0 = 1'); sql/where.py WhereNode.as_sql (appends '1=1' instead of decrementing empty_needed); added reproduce_error.py.
Outcome: Passed the issue's tests but wider tests and review later found it wrong; no failing test is on record.
Why it failed: Inferred: the where.py and compiler.py checks match any negated WhereNode whose single child has empty_result_set_value, which every expression and lookup has. A negated node that raises EmptyResultSet (matches nothing) is then turned into "always true", so the query returns all rows instead of none.
Lesson: Handle the empty subquery inside Exists/WhereNode logic itself. Never use guesses about tree shape or hasattr in the compiler that turn "matches nothing" into "matches everything".
5ecb7f1b2e:
Changed: No Django source. The patch only adds a new script, reproduce_error.py, which shows the bug: two ProfileForm instances share one error_messages dict. django/forms/fields.py and Field.__deepcopy__ are untouched.
Outcome: The fix passed the project's tests for this issue, but wider tests and review later found it wrong: it does not resolve the issue, and no failing test is on record.
Why it failed: Inferred: Field.__deepcopy__ still makes a shallow copy, so every deep-copied field keeps pointing at the same error_messages dict. A change to one form instance's field error messages still shows up in every other instance.
Lesson: A correct fix must change Field.__deepcopy__ in django/forms/fields.py so that each copy gets its own deep copy of error_messages. A patch that only adds scripts or tests does not fix it.
619ff87ff9:
Changed: sphinx/domains/python.py: added _split_at_commas_outside_parentheses_and_braces and used it in _pseudo_parse_arglist in place of arglist.split(','). Also pinned dependencies in setup.py, edited tox.ini, and added python.py.backup plus many scratch scripts.
Outcome: Rejected: it failed the project's tests for this issue.

Lesson: The fix must make sphinx.pycode.ast unparse wrap a non-empty Tuple in parentheses, while "()" still gives "()". Patching only the signature splitting in the Python domain is not enough. Leave out dependency pins, backup files and scratch scripts.
63f4b0d89b:
Changed: django/http/response.py HttpResponseBase.delete_cookie (new secure/httponly/samesite params); contrib/messages/storage/cookie.py CookieStorage._update_cookie; contrib/sessions/middleware.py SessionMiddleware.process_response; also added stray files (response.py.backup, test_*.py, verify_fix.py).

The session tests (test_session_delete_on_end*) expect the exact header "...Path=/; SameSite=Lax"; the patch also passes httponly, adding HttpOnly.

640667fbee:
Changed: sympy/ntheory/residue_ntheory.py nthroot_mod: an early return of 0 (or [0]) whenever a % p == 0, before every other check. Also added scratch scripts and .backup copies.
Outcome: Rejected; it failed the project's tests for this issue.

653934b8d6:
Changed: django/db/models/fields/__init__.py, Field.get_prep_value (base class): unwraps SimpleLazyObject via _setupfunc/_wrapped and turns any object with _meta into its .pk.
Outcome: Passed the issue's tests but wider tests and review later found it wrong; no failing test is on record.
Why it failed: Inferred: LazyObject.__init__ always sets _wrapped (to the `empty` sentinel), so `hasattr(value, '_wrapped')` is always true and _setup() never runs; an unevaluated lazy object becomes `empty`. Changing every field to turn model instances into pk also hides the real problem (the nested Subquery's output_field is the wrong field) and ignores to_field.
Lesson: A correct fix must work for a lazy object that has not been evaluated yet. It must not add a model-to-pk conversion to the base Field.get_prep_value for all fields. The nested subquery annotation should resolve to the relation field.
6aec55046e:
Changed: sphinx/builders/linkcheck.py: CheckExternalLinksBuilder.write_doc, plus a new check_local_link, defined twice. Also setup.py pins, tox.ini, and many stray scripts and backup files.
Outcome: Rejected; it failed the project's tests for this issue (test_defaults, test_anchors_ignored).
Why it failed: Inferred: local links are checked synchronously, outside the worker/check() path, so linkcheck_ignore is skipped and 'path/to/notfound' is still reported broken. Paths resolve against the process's working directory, not srcdir, so conf.py can be flagged broken. Both target and reference nodes are checked, so entries are duplicated and the output.txt line count breaks.
Lesson: Classify local URIs inside the existing check() flow, after the ignore patterns. Resolve paths against srcdir/the document's directory. Report each link once. Write a "[broken] <uri>" entry only for missing files.
6d5509c9fa:
Changed: Only added a new file, reproduce_error.py (a test model plus the functions execQuery and execQueryWithoutWrapper that print SQL). No Django source file or function was changed.
Outcome: The fix passed the project's tests for this issue but wider tests and review later found it wrong, so it does not resolve the issue. No failing test is on record.
Why it failed: Inferred: Django's code is unchanged, so ExpressionWrapper(Value(3)) used inside values().annotate(Sum(...)) still puts the constant "3" in GROUP BY, and Postgres still fails.
Lesson: A correct fix must change Django's GROUP BY handling (django/db/models) so that an ExpressionWrapper around a constant adds no GROUP BY column. A wrapped non-constant expression must still be grouped. A script that only reproduces the bug does not count as a fix.
6d57904897:
Changed: astropy/units/format/cds.py (p_combined_units, p_division_of_units, p_product_of_units rewritten as left-recursive grammar), regenerated astropy/units/format/cds_parsetab.py, and pinned setuptools==68.0.0 in pyproject.toml.
Outcome: The fix was rejected because it failed the project's tests for this issue (at least one decisive test failed or an existing test broke).
Why it failed: Inferred: the rule "division_of_units DIVISION product_of_units" lets a product follow a slash, so "km/s.Mpc-1" (and "/s.Mpc") parse instead of raising, contrary to test_cds_grammar_fail[km/s.Mpc-1]; which test_cds_grammar cases (strings4, strings6) failed is not shown.
Lesson: Chained divisions must apply left to right (km/s/Mpc = km/(s.Mpc), 10+3J/m/s/kpc2 = 1e3 W/(m kpc2)), "/s" must parse, and a bare product after a slash (km/s.Mpc-1, /s.Mpc) must still be rejected.
6ea3388049:
Changed: sympy/tensor/array/dense_ndim_array.py (ImmutableDenseNDimArray._new and MutableDenseNDimArray._new) and sympy/tensor/array/sparse_ndim_array.py (ImmutableSparseNDimArray.__new__ and MutableSparseNDimArray.__new__). Why it failed: Inferred: `_loop_size` also bounds integer index checks, so a scalar array probably now accepts `a[0]` and returns the element instead of raising. The empty-tuple index `a[()]` is the only valid one.
Lesson: A correct fix makes len() of a rank-0 array 1 for dense and sparse, mutable and immutable arrays. It keeps a[()] returning the scalar and a[0] raising ValueError. It adds no scratch files.
6f6e19ad5a:
Changed: sympy/printing/repr.py, which got new ReprPrinter._print_set and _print_dict methods. The fix also added two scratch scripts at the repository root, edge_cases.py and reproduce_error.py.
Outcome: The fix passed the project's tests for this issue but wider tests and review later found it wrong, and no failing test is on record.
Why it failed: Inferred: srepr(set()) prints "{}", which evaluates back to a dict, not a set. Set and dict elements print in hash or insertion order rather than a stable sorted order, so the output is not deterministic. frozenset is not handled.
Lesson: A correct fix must make srepr of an empty set print "set()". It must print set and dict elements in a stable sorted order (for example by default_sort_key) and print every key and value through srepr. It must not leave scratch scripts in the repository.
715077e2d1:
Changed: sympy/core/function.py, Function._eval_evalf (the _imp_ fallback branch); also added a scratch script test_evalf.py at the repo root.
Outcome: The fix passed the issue's tests but wider tests and review later found it wrong; no failing test is on record.
Why it failed: Inferred: it calls arg.evalf(prec) and result.evalf(prec) with prec, which is binary precision in _eval_evalf, as if it were decimal digits. It also turns args into Floats before calling _imp_, so _imp_ never sees exact values. When the result stays symbolic it returns that expression where it should return None.

Changed: xarray/core/computation.py, where(): added a keep_attrs=None parameter (defaulting to _get_keep_attrs(default=False)) and passed it to apply_ufunc.

Changed: django/apps/registry.py Apps.get_app_config (adds a case-insensitive label fallback); django/db/models/fields/related.py resolve_relation (rewrites explicit "app.Model" strings through get_app_config); adds a stray reproduce_error.py.

9d31a3aa67:
Changed: django/db/models/lookups.py, Lookup.get_prep_lookup (now unwraps the value when _wrapped is a Promise and replaces any object with _meta by its pk); also added a stray reproduce_error.py at the repository root.

Changed: django/db/models/sql/query.py, Query.split_exclude(): the inner query became self.clone() instead of Query(self.model). It also added a stray reproduce_issue.py at the repo root.
Outcome: The fix passed the project's tests for this issue, but wider tests and review later found it wrong; no failing test is on record.
Why it failed: Inferred: cloning the whole outer query copies its WHERE filters, annotations, select list, joins and alias refcounts, limits and distinct into the exclude subquery. The subquery is then no longer a clean "pk IN (...)" query: outer conditions get duplicated, and trim_start can work on the wrong joins.
Lesson: split_exclude must still build a fresh inner Query(self.model) and copy only the FilteredRelation definitions (_filtered_relations), so the annotation name resolves. Inherited filters, joins and annotations must stay out of the subquery.
fc68ffbbc7:
Changed: astropy/io/fits/card.py _format_float (now tries str(value) first and falls back to f"{value:.16G}"); adds a stray reproduce.py.
Outcome: The fix passed the issue's tests but wider tests and review later found it wrong; no failing test is on record.
Why it failed: Inferred: str() writes a lowercase 'e' with no '.' for values like 1e-05 or 1e+20. The '.0' check only looks for uppercase 'E', so it turns these into '1e-05.0'. The exponent split then calls int('05.0') and raises ValueError, so such cards can no longer be built.
Lesson: Use the shortest round-trip repr only when it fits in 20 characters. Normalize the exponent to uppercase 'E' with two digits before any decimal-point check, never append '.0' to exponent forms, and keep the .16G fallback and truncation.

Why it failed: Inferred: the patch only reorders checks in Float.__eq__. A zero Float still returns "not other" for any falsy non-Boolean object instead of comparing it as a number. The patch also leaves a debug script in the repository.
Lesson: A correct fix must give S(0.0) == S.false and S.false == S(0.0) the same result (False), with no truthiness shortcut in Float.__eq__. It must not add scratch files.
